prompt: Reverse-extracted from an existing KiCad project (Astra_Computer_V2.kicad_pcb / .kicad_sch) rather than generated from a text prompt. Board is a dual-coprocessor rocketry flight computer: ESP32-S3 main MCU + Wi-Fi/BLE telemetry, dual redundant ATmega4808 coprocessors, BNO085 9-DOF IMU, I3G4250D gyroscope, ADXL375 high-g accelerometer, BMP581 barometric altimeter, u-blox MIA-M10Q GPS, SST26VF032B SPI flash + SD storage, dual AP63203WU buck regulators (isolated CPU vs sensor rails), 6x pyro/recovery deployment channels, RGB status LEDs, buzzer, and USB-C.

input_source.note: VIN net feeds both buck regulators U8 and U9 directly; source battery chemistry/voltage not encoded in PCB/schematic netlist — verify against Power Reg sheet notes

rails.note: Raw input rail distributed to both regulator channels and to external connectors/pyro switching FET Q2
Sensor/logic rail — powers gyro, flash, coprocessor 1 & 2, baro, GPS, BNO085 IMU
Dedicated, separately-regulated rail isolating the ESP32-S3 (Wi-Fi/BLE RF + digital switching noise) from the sensitive sensor rail (+3V3) — deliberate noise-isolation architecture
Filtered RF supply tap (via R35 and associated LC filtering) for the u-blox GPS module's RF front end, separated from digital +3V3 to reduce GNSS receiver noise floor

_NEW_power_tree.regulator_topology_note: Dual independent AP63203WU buck regulators (U8, U9) split the design into a CPU/RF rail (+CPU3V3, ESP32-S3 only) and a sensor/logic rail (+3V3, everything else) — a deliberate power-domain isolation strategy typical of flight computers to keep Wi-Fi/BLE switching noise out of the IMU/baro/gyro measurement chain. No power budget (mA/µA per rail) is present in the KiCad source files — would require BOM current specs + duty cycle analysis to populate power_budget_table.

placement_constraints.note: Keep BNO085 orientation sensor away from ESP32-S3 RF/switching activity
BMP581 should be placed near a vent hole/enclosure opening for accurate ambient pressure sensing

placement_rules_text.text: Keep the ESP32-S3 (U1) crystal (Y1) within 5mm with short symmetric traces — long or asymmetric crystal traces degrade RF/clock stability.

Keep each buck regulator's inductor (U8/L1, U9/L4) tight to the IC to minimize switching-node loop area and radiated EMI, which is critical given the sensitive IMU/gyro/baro sensors sharing this board.

Physically separate the ESP32-S3 RF section and its +CPU3V3 rail from the sensor cluster (U2 gyro, U5 baro, U6 accel, U10 IMU) — this separation is already reflected in the dual-rail power architecture and should carry through to placement.

Route pyro/recovery channel traces (TRG/SENSE/RET, driven by Q1-Q8) away from the IMU/gyro/baro sensor cluster and I2C buses — high-current switching transients during deployment should not couple into sensor readings.
Keep the GPS RF path (VCC_RF, /GPS/RF, /GPS/RF_B) short and away from digital switching nets and the buck converter switching nodes to preserve GNSS receiver sensitivity.

topology_details.description: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U serves as the primary flight computer / telemetry MCU on an isolated +CPU3V3 rail. Two redundant ATmega4808 coprocessors (COPRO1, COPRO2) independently handle time-critical pyro/recovery channel logic. Sensor suite (BNO085 9-DOF fusion IMU, I3G4250D gyroscope, ADXL375 high-g accelerometer, BMP581 barometric altimeter, MIA-M10Q GPS) shares a separate +3V3 rail, isolated from CPU/RF noise via dual AP63203WU buck regulators. SST26VF032B SPI flash plus an SD card interface (SDStorage sheet) provide onboard data logging. Six pyro/recovery channels (TRG1-6, SENSE1-6, RET1-6) are switched via discrete MOSFETs (Q1-Q8) for parachute/recovery deployment.
